content.text:
The pattern is best explained by the monoclinic V2O3 candidate (mp-715514) alone. This rests on approximate d-spacing matching, not a full simulation of each candidate's pattern.

1. **No low-angle peaks.** Nothing appears below about 23° two-theta. That argues against the large or low-symmetry cells (BaWO4, Rb5Au3O2, Na3NiO3), which should all have reflections lower down.
2. **Spinel ruled out.** ZnGa2O4 has a cubic cell of about 8.46 Å. Its main reflections would sit near 18.2°, 29.9°, 35.2° and 42.7°. There are no peaks at 18° or 30°.
3. **Double perovskites and trirutile do not fit.**
   - Ca2NdRuO6 would put its first strong reflections near 21.8–21.9°, but the observed first peak is at 23.3°.
   - Sr2CaSbO6 has a larger pseudo-cubic cell (about 4.2 Å), so its main peak would fall near 30°, which is absent.
   - VFeSbO6 (trirutile) would give a strong rutile-type peak near 27.2°, which is also absent.
4. **Monoclinic V2O3 fits.** I compared with corundum V2O3 spacings, expanded about 3% as is typical for these computed cells.

| Corundum reflection | Expected d / position | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| (012) | d ≈ 3.76 Å | 23.3–24.5° |
| (104) | ≈ 32.1° | split triplet at 31.9–32.7° |
| (110) | ≈ 35° | doublet at 34.1/34.6° (the 100-intensity peak) |
| (113) | ≈ 40° | 40.2–40.8° |
| (116) | ≈ 52.5° | 52.3° |

The splitting of the corundum-type peaks into doublets and triplets is what the monoclinic distortion would produce. The (024) match is less clean: expected near 48.4°, while the observed peaks there are at 46.2, 46.6 and 47.6°.

I found no peaks that require a second phase.
